newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker, hurt by strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker, hurt by strong U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Friday, softening with U.S. treasuries after the release of stronger than expected U.S. employment data for July.

"It's the stronger than expected payroll number, but some of the details of the report weren't as strong as what was implied by the headline number," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "The initial reaction was not as negative as you would have thought on that headline number."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.31 to C$122.37 to yield 6.322 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 17/32 to yield 6.34 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to two basis points from one basis point at Thursday's close.

North American fixed-income markets weakened on Friday after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the economy added 316,000 jobs in July and the jobless rate stood at 4.8 percent. Economists had forecast non-farm payrolls growth of 193,000 and a jobless rate of 4.9 percent.
But analysts said the underlying report was not as strong as the headline numbers implied, which helped temper the selloff.
Chandler said the fact that some of the employment gains came in the the public sector helped offset market concern about the report's strength.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.30 to C$110.61 to yield 5.815 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 17/32 to yield 6.08 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 27 basis points from 23 basis points at Thursday's close.
